content:
Asha: Heads-up — seeing recurring inter-node RTT jumps in the gpu-pool during today's 11:30-12:15 PST batching window. Latency goes from ~0.8ms -> 6-25ms for a few minutes, every 3-5 min burst. Graph: https://grafana.redwood/sys/cluster/gpu-e2e
Tom: Uptime/packetloss? any drops or RX errs on the NICs?
Asha: Packet loss counters tiny but there are growing RX missed packets on ixgbevf children. No full link flaps. Logs attached below.
Miguel: Can you run an iperf3 between two affected nodes when it's spiking? Also get ethtool -S for the physical NIC.
Asha: Ran quick iperf3 during a spike — saw jitter and throughput collapse on the east-west path.

Asha: ```
# iperf3 -c gpunode-07
[  5]  0.00-10.00  sec  1.2 GBytes  1.02 Gbits/sec  jitter 4.6 ms  lost/total 12/10000 (0.12%)
```

Sophie: Any recent firmware/driver rollouts in that region? Could be a replay of the NIC RX ring sizing/firmware mismatch we saw months ago.
Miguel: Checking deployment history... nic-fw 2.4.1 rolled out two weeks ago to eu-west-gpu pool. Driver kernel module 5.14 patched on nodes two days ago.
Kai: Also saw similar pattern in staging when jobs synchronized heavy KV-cache fills — synchronized bursts can cause QoS/ECMP path oscillation. Are batching windows aligned across many pods?
Asha: Yes, many pods hit the same prefix-cache checkpoint ~every 3 min due to aligned checkpointing and scheduled maintenance tasks.
Tom: Hypothesis: bursty east-west traffic + ECMP path hashing changes + NIC/FW backpressure => transient queuing on certain ToRs -> RTT spikes.
Sophie: Can we test mitigations: 1) stagger batch checkpoints, 2) temporary enable jumbo frames (MTU 9000) on a canary pair, 3) increase NIC Rx ring, 4) pin ECMP hashing to flow-based? Small canary rollout first.
Miguel: I can patch a canary pair with sysctl and ethtool changes: ```sysctl -w net.core.netdev_max_backlog=50000; ethtool -G eth0 rx 4096 tx 512``` then monitor.
infra-bot: Canary change request created: CR-4129. Schedule window 22:00 UTC.
Kai: Also add netem experiment to emulate bursts locally before rolling to prod: tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 10ms 5ms distribution normal
Asha: Doing a quick test now on canary-03 — will report back after next batching window.
Tom: Thanks. If canary looks good, plan to roll firmware-driver combo rollback or Rx ring bump across affected ToRs and add traffic shaping as longer term.
Sophie: Action items: Miguel to run canary + collect ethtool/systat; Asha to coordinate job-stagger config with infra-scheduler; Kai to run netem preflight tests. Target: mitigation roll by EOD tomorrow.
Asha: OK started metrics collection. Posting full ethtool and NIC counters once window completes.
Miguel: FYI I saw a CQE overflow hint in dmesg on one host during spike — grabbing logs now.
Asha: Thanks team :thumbsup:
